summary: A string of points that each open by addressing a different group.
realLife: Kennedy's inaugural has six in a row opening on the same address to a different set of nations; Reagan and Obama have shorter runs.
sources: docs/story/research/address-moves.md (Elections lane, Nov 24, 2026: 6 inaugurals and 6 State of the State addresses read whole, 175 points coded)
inGame: Shape `address-run` in the `call` section, with `address-to` pieces gated on the-disaster, run-jobs-lost, run-prices-ahead, run-span and term-left.

turns.what: One group is singled out, not a run.
turns.pulledBy: a short speech; few story facts (no disaster, no run flags)
turns.writesBack: One person or group hears itself named; that group's later talk can bring it up.

turns.what: The run comes at the close, as a thank-you to each group.
turns.pulledBy: a speaker who thanks (polite, humble); a good year
turns.writesBack: Each group named is a line the housemate or paper can repeat.
